name: TerribleSettingsAuditor
description: Screens a .NET app's configuration with TSA (tsa --screen --json) and publishes tsa-report.json to the TSA tab.
author: mrjamiebowman

inputs.name: path
inputs.label: App DLL or executable
inputs.helpMarkDown: Path to the app that references TerribleSettingsAuditor. A `.dll` is run with `dotnet`; anything else is run directly. Minimatch patterns are allowed (e.g. `**/publish/MyApp.dll`) as long as they match exactly one file.

inputs.name: noJoke
inputs.label: No Joke
inputs.helpMarkDown: Passes `--no-joke` so TSA keeps its sense of humour to itself.

inputs.name: quiet
inputs.label: Quiet
inputs.helpMarkDown: Passes `--quiet` to hide the TSA banner.

inputs.name: failOnScreeningFailure
inputs.label: Fail the task when screening fails
inputs.helpMarkDown: When off, a failed screening marks the task as 'succeeded with issues' instead of failed.

inputs.name: workingDirectory
inputs.label: Working directory
inputs.helpMarkDown: Directory the app runs in. Defaults to the app's own directory so `appsettings.json` is found.

inputs.name: reportPath
inputs.label: Report file
inputs.helpMarkDown: Where TSA writes its JSON report, relative to the working directory.

inputs.name: timeoutInSeconds
inputs.label: Timeout (seconds)
inputs.helpMarkDown: Kills the app if it hasn't exited by then (e.g. it ignored the `tsa` argument and started serving). 0 disables the timeout.

outputVariables.name: TsaPassed
outputVariables.description: 'true' when every screened setting passed, otherwise 'false'.

outputVariables.name: TsaReportPath
outputVariables.description: Full path to the tsa-report.json that was published.
